title: Micro-shift Rotation and Regulatory Evidence Cadence
author: Lena Torres
content:
Overview
========
This page documents a lightweight, repeatable on-call cadence optimized for short, high-focus shifts ("micro-shifts") paired with a mandatory regulatory evidence capture workflow. The goal is to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for fast-moving transient incidents, preserve high-quality forensic artifacts for customers in regulated industries, and provide concise, reusable status and customer communication templates.

Scope
-----
Applies to: SRE, Serving Runtime, Incident Operators, Customer Success for regulated customers.
Not in scope: long-term capacity planning (see eng-sre/capacity-planning).

Why this approach
------------------
- Many modern inference incidents (throttles, noisy neighbors, cache storming) appear and resolve within tens of minutes. Traditional 8-hour handoff windows increase context-switching and fatigue.
- Micro-shifts (2–3 hour focused windows) reduce responder fatigue, improve signal isolation, and make evidence collection consistent.
- Regulated customers require preserved evidence (logs, traces, rolling metrics) with clear retention and access controls.

Key concepts
------------
- Micro-shift: a 2-hour primary coverage window with a designated operator (Primary). Secondary is a 4-hour backup.
- Evidence bundle: time-bounded artifact set (logs, traces, profile snapshots, KV cache state summaries) stored in a secure artifacts bucket with an immutable manifest.
- Choreography: predetermined status page and customer-comm templates with variable placeholders and escalation cadence.

Rotation schedule (example)
--------------------------
- Day splits: 08:00–10:00, 10:00–12:00, 12:00–14:00, ... up to 20:00–22:00. Night coverage uses 4-hour blocks 22:00–02:00 / 02:00–06:00.
- Handoff overlap: 5 minutes of overlap required; slack handoff not allowed.
- Escalation: if Primary cannot stabilize within the 30-minute triage window, Secondary takes over and Primary prepares evidence bundle.

Roles & responsibilities
------------------------
- Primary (on-micro-shift): first responder; owns triage and initial containment.
- Secondary: backup and escalation; supports confidence checks and can assume bridge operator role.
- Bridge Operator: coordinates cross-team comms and executes customer notifications.
- Evidence Steward (on-call rotation, weekly): ensures artifacts are uploaded to secure storage and manifest is complete for regulatory customers.

Runbook invocation (quick checklist)
-----------------------------------
1) Acknowledge page in PagerDuty and set status: "Investigating".
2) Quick triage (10 mins): confirm whether incident impacts model inference throughput or quality.
3) If impact > customer SLA or persistent after 10 mins, invoke evidence capture (step 4).
4) Execute evidence capture script and upload artifacts.
5) Notify Bridge Operator and prepare customer-safe status.

Evidence capture: required artifact list
-------------------------------------
- System logs: /var/log/serving/*.log covering +5m before alarm to +5m after resolution.
- Tracing snapshot: distributed trace for the incident window (trace IDs).
- Metrics export: prometheus range query for 30m window centered on alert (JSON).
- KV cache snapshot: top-100 entries and cache hit/miss rates.
- Model variant mapping: model name + commit hash + quantization profile in use.
- Operator console transcript: CLI history for actions taken during triage.

Capture commands (examples)
--------------------------
- Metrics: curl -s "https://prometheus/api/v1/query_range?query=redwood_serving_latency_seconds_bucket&start=${START}&end=${END}&step=15s" > metrics-${INCIDENT_ID}.json
- Traces: rtrace export --service serving --start ${START} --end ${END} --out traces-${INCIDENT_ID}.json
- Logs: tar -czf logs-${INCIDENT_ID}.tgz /var/log/serving/ --since "${START}" --until "${END}"
- KV snapshot: ./tools/kv-dump --top 100 > kv-${INCIDENT_ID}.json

Artifact manifest (plain text example)
------------------------------------
Incident-ID: ${INCIDENT_ID}
Start: ${START}
End: ${END}
Artifacts:
- metrics-${INCIDENT_ID}.json (prometheus)
- traces-${INCIDENT_ID}.json (jaeger/rtrace)
- logs-${INCIDENT_ID}.tgz (system logs)
- kv-${INCIDENT_ID}.json (kv cache snapshot)
- modelmap-${INCIDENT_ID}.txt (model metadata)
Uploader: ${PRIMARY_NAME}
Bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/${CUSTOMER_ID}/${INCIDENT_ID}/

Retention and access controls
-----------------------------
- Retain evidence for regulated customers for 2 years by default; auto-archive to cold storage after 90 days.
- Access: Evidence Stewards and Security may request read access; `evidence-read` IAM role required.
- Deletion: Only Security and Legal can approve deletion; process described in security-and-compliance/audits.

Status page choreography templates
--------------------------------
(Use these verbatim in the status page UI with variable replacement)
1) Initial "Investigating" stub:
Title: Investigating increased inference latency in {region}
Body: We are investigating elevated latency affecting a subset of inference requests in {region}. Impact: degraded latency for some customers. Next update: {ETA_15_MIN}.
2) Update "Mitigating" stub:
Title: Mitigation in progress — routing changes deployed
Body: We have deployed routing changes and are observing reduced tail latency. Impact: partial. Next update: {ETA_30_MIN}.
3) Resolve stub:
Title: Resolved — inference latency normalized
Body: The issue was resolved by routing to healthy capacity and applying cache warmup. Customers may have seen errors between {START} and {END}. If you continue to see issues, contact support@redwood.com.

Customer communication templates (regulated tone)
-----------------------------------------------
- Severity P1 initial (external-ready):
Subject: Redwood — Incident impacting inference latency (Customer Impact Possible)
Body: Hello {CustomerName},
We detected an event affecting inference latency between {START} and {END}. We are actively investigating and capturing a regulatory evidence bundle. We will provide an update by {ETA_15_MIN}.
Regards,
Redwood Incident Team

- Follow-up (evidence available):
Subject: Incident update and evidence package — {Incident-ID}
Body: Hello {CustomerName},
We have completed our initial investigation and uploaded an evidence bundle to s3://redwood-evidence/{CustomerID}/{Incident-ID}/. The bundle contains logs, traces, metrics, cache snapshot, and model metadata. If you require additional detail or a conference call, please reply and we will schedule.

Game-day scenario (micro-shift simulation)
-----------------------------------------
Purpose: validate that micro-shifts + evidence capture finish within a 30-minute window and that artifacts meet regulatory minimums.
Simulated incident: sudden KV cache thrash causing 30% increase in tail latency and 5xx errors for a single model variant.
Exercise steps:
1) Trigger synthetic traffic to reproduce elevated miss rate.
2) Primary acknowledges within 2 minutes; performs quick triage.
3) Evidence Steward runs capture commands and uploads artifacts.
4) Secondary coordinates with Bridge and runs mitigation (increase routing weight to variant v1.3).
5) Declare mitigate and run post-scan to ensure no residual 5xx.
Success criteria:
- Evidence bundle exists and manifest completed < 30m.
- Status page posted at Investigating + Mitigating + Resolved with correct timestamps.
- Postmortem starter doc created within 48h.

Post-incident lightweight postmortem template
-------------------------------------------
- Title: <Short description>
- Incident ID: <ID>
- Impact: affected customers, SLA deviations, duration
- Timeline: bulletized minute-level events for first 60 minutes, then coarser granularity
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence pointers (artifact URLs)
- Action items: owner, ETA, risk level
- Regulatory evidence confirmation: link to S3 manifest and steward sign-off

Escalation matrix (one-line table)
--------------------------------
Role | Primary contact | Pager duty group | Escalation threshold
Primary | On-call micro-shift | pd-oncall-primary | immediate
Secondary | On-call backup | pd-oncall-secondary | if > 30m unresolved
Bridge | Bridge Operator | pd-bridge | any customer-impacting incident
Security | Security on-call | pd-security | if evidence tampering suspected

Operational knobs and SLOs to monitor
-------------------------------------
- 99th latency (inference): target < 1200ms across 99th for hosted customers. Alert if 99th > 2000ms for 5m.
- 5xx rate: alert if > 0.5% rolling 10m.
- Cache miss amplification: alert if cache miss ratio increases 3x baseline for 5m.

Automation & utilities
---------------------
- PagerDuty runbook integration: each incident trigger automatically runs a Lambda that creates an Incident record and prepopulates the Evidence manifest with start timestamp.
- Evidence uploader: CLI tool with `evidence upload --incident ${ID} --bucket s3://...` that writes a final manifest and sets ACLs.
- Status page API: /status/api/v1/incidents accepts JSON payloads for quick status updates. Example payload: `{"id":"${ID}","state":"investigating","message":"{msg}"}`

Training and game-day cadence
----------------------------
- Quarterly micro-shift game days (2-hour simulation blocks) with a required Evidence Steward present.
- New responders must shadow 3 micro-shifts and pass a synthetic evidence capture lab.

Metrics & Reporting
-------------------
- Weekly: number of micro-shift escalations, mean evidence manifest time (creation -> upload), number of artifacts with missing data.
- Quarterly: regulatory readiness score for each customer (artifact completeness and access audit).

Appendices
----------
A. Quick CLI cheat-sheet:
- Start window vars: START=$(date -u -d '-5 minutes' +%s) ; END=$(date -u +%s)
- tar logs: tar -czf logs-${INCIDENT_ID}.tgz /var/log/serving/ --newer-mtime=@${START} --files-from=/dev/null

B. Contacts
- Primary roster: https://okta.redwood.com/app/team/oncall (internal)
- Evidence stewarding policy: security-and-compliance/evidence-retention

C. Frequently asked questions
Q: Who owns evidence billing for storage?
A: Evidence storage is charged to the owning product line; steward flags and cost center are in the manifest.
